old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-s61e","title":"Python slot claim: sibling payload fields (slots elements, superframe_epoch, expiry, ordinal) lack upper bounds — same bignum/oversized divergence class as jkuj","description":"Codereview finding (jkuj security pass, reviewer kimi-k3). The jkuj fix bounds claim_seq at u32::MAX, but the same cbor2-bignum divergence remains open on the other SlotClaim payload fields. At decode (python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py): slots elements checked only for int-ness (:240-243); superframe_epoch (:245), expiry (:255), ordinal (:267) checked int+non-negative only — all unbounded above. Rust bounds each: per-slot u32::try_from (slot.rs:574) plus count \u003c= MAX_SLOTS_PER_SUPERFRAME and per-slot \u003c slots_per_superframe; superframe_epoch/expiry/ordinal read as u64 (slot.rs:579/581/592), so CBOR tag-2 bignums above 2**64-1 are MalformedClaim. Consequence: a gateway-key holder can sign a claim carrying slots=[2**100] or superframe_epoch=2**100; Python verifies the signature and advances the replay high-water while every Rust peer discards identical bytes as malformed — the same cross-implementation replay-state poisoning class as jkuj. __post_init__ has the same gaps (:168-178). Minimal fix: bound slot elements to 0 \u003c= s \u003c= 0xFFFFFFFF (or slots_per_superframe ceiling where known) and the three scalar fields to 0 \u003c= v \u003c= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at both validation sites, matching Rust decode ranges. Distinct from jkuj (claim_seq, now fixed) and from qpco.5 (bit-exact CBOR parity sweep, broader).","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-09T01:53:52.137847712Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-09-09T01:53:52.137847712Z","labels":["python","gateway"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-s61e","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-jkuj","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-09-09T01:53:52.404656082Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
